title: analytics: the ObjectQL /analytics/sql echo prints IN / = SQL for a multi-value-field filter the engine refuses with 400
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by the #35270 review sweep (run record r08 S6) on PR #36184, re-read on main c30ce97cd7

## What happens
The analytics "show me the SQL" endpoint prints a normal-looking SQL statement for a filter that the platform will actually refuse to run. When a report filters a multi-value field (tags, multi-select) with equality or "in", the real query answers 400, but on the ObjectQL path the SQL preview answers 200 with a plain `IN (...)` statement. An author who copies that SQL, or trusts the preview, is misled about what the report does.

- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts:2207` `buildFilterClauseSql`: `in` / `notIn` print `col IN (...)` / `NOT IN (...)` (`:2249-2254`) and the plain comparisons below, with no declared-shape check; reached from `generateSql` (`:916`) via `renderFilterNodeSql` (`:1184`).
- The same file states the echo's contract: the echo and the executed statement are one description, and "an echo that printed a parseable statement while the engine refused the real one is that failure in its loudest form" (`:2286-2290`).
- The native strategy refuses the same leaf (`native-sql-strategy.ts:2510`), so the same `/analytics/sql` request answers 400 on one strategy and a 200 echo on the other. Pre-existing on the ObjectQL side.

## Done when
- The ObjectQL echo refuses a leaf of `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` on a declared multi-value / JSON-stored column with the same `400 INVALID_FILTER` and sentence (reuse `json-column-comparison-refusal.ts`).
- Pins: `/analytics/sql` (ObjectQL strategy) with `{ tags: { $in: ['a'] } }` on a `multiple: true` field → 400; `$nin`, implicit equality → 400; control: `$contains` and a scalar `$in` → 200 with SQL.
- Ablation: remove the refusal call from the echo and the `$in` pin goes red.

reach: public HTTP door `POST /api/v1/analytics/sql` on the ObjectQL strategy; display only, runs nothing. Read from the code, not measured.
Business reason: report authors see SQL that claims to work for a filter the platform rejects, so they debug the wrong thing.
Reader: area:reports / domain:server (service-analytics).
Dedupe: `analytics sql echo`, `objectql strategy echo`, `36184` → #33878, #36189, #36190 (none carries this).
Grade: p3 — preview text only; the real query is refused correctly.
